reason: A trunked plant has a trunk. Trunk present fits.
Tuberous-thickened describes a root or rhizome thickened like a tuber, so tuberous fits.
Ultramarine is a shade of blue.
The PATO synonym for plicate is pleated, so unpleated means not plicate.
Weakly distinct means hardly visible, which is close to inconspicuous. Weaker than a plain 'indistinct'.
Without horns means not horned.
The rule drops 'median'. A part with no median groove can still have other grooves, but 'not grooved' says it has none at all. Keep it as a phrase or reject it.
PO leaf midvein is only for leaves. A midrib is also found on sepals, lemmas, phyllaries and other parts.
Without perianth means perianth absent.
Sterile stamens are staminodes, so a missing ring of them means staminodes are absent.
'Wooded' describes land with trees, which is habitat. The word for a plant part is 'woody'. Reject it.
Amethyst is a violet-purple colour.
Aperturate means a pollen grain has apertures, which are germination openings. Perforate means pierced by holes. Use pollen aperture present if needed, otherwise reject.
Bearing scales means scaly.
Bent upward means upturned.
A blunt-pointed apex is obtuse.
Broad-cuneate is a wide-angled cuneate base. The target keeps the main shape.
This is a comparison of width against length (transversely broader). 'Broad' loses that. Probably a typo for 'broader than long'. Reject or make a specific rule.
Ligulate means tongue- or strap-shaped.
A typo for capitate.
PO lists catkin as a synonym of catkin inflorescence. A bare 'catkin' states that one is present.
Cinnabar is a bright red-orange, which is vermilion.
Cirrhose means ending in or bearing a tendril, so tendrilous.
Arranged corymbosely means corymb-like.
Covered by an aril means an aril is present.
Creased is close to wrinkled. Weaker than a plain 'wrinkled'.
Cupiform means cup-shaped.
Cuspless means without a cusp, so not cuspidate.
A scorpioid cyme is a cymose type, so scorpioid keeps the main meaning.
PO lists dichasium as a synonym of cyme inflorescence.
Discernible means can be seen, not that it stands out. It is weaker than conspicuous. Reject.
Distinctive means characteristic. It does not mean conspicuous. Reject. (Distinct for veins is different.)
In grasses, dorsally compressed means flattened on the back, so dorso-ventrally flattened.
Equal-sided means symmetrical, as in a leaf base.
Feeble stems or branches are weak, and the rule is already limited to stem|branch.
The adverb is only a degree word. The reticulate pattern is kept.
'Finely' is lost. The target says only that veins are present. Reject, or map to vein present with a fineness value.
Fusoid means spindle-shaped, which is fusiform.
Fuzzed means covered with fuzz, so hairy.
A spelling variant of glabrescent.
Glomerulose means in small dense clusters, so aggregated.
Gradually narrowing means tapered.
Half-rounded means half-round, so semicircular. The wording is ambiguous.
Innate means attached by the base only for anthers. Elsewhere it means inherent or inborn.
The adverb is only a degree word. Laciniate is kept.
The irregularity is lost, and oval is not always elliptic. Reject, or use an irregular shape term.
The adverb is only a degree word. Reticulate is kept.
Isotomous branching is equal forking, which is bifurcated.
PO secondary leaf vein is for leaves only. Lateral veins also occur on sepals, petals, bracts and lemmas.
Straw-coloured is a PATO synonym of straw yellow. 'Light' is lost, but the colour is the same.
